answer: In an agent market trading pigments such as umber, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days to receive one daily bid slot. Slots scale with bonded capital, so splitting funds among a tide of fake agents yields no extra bidding power. Creating 1,000 identities requires locking $100,000 for a month, imposing financing costs and tying up funds the attacker could use elsewhere. Cheap names alone become a hollow advantage.
